response:
Here's the SKILL.md. I changed four things from your paste, explained below.

```markdown
---
name: release-notes
description: Invoke when the user asks to write, draft, or post release notes or a changelog for a new version. Collect commits since the last tag, group feat/fix/perf, put breaking changes first, keep under 150 words in customer language, then confirm before running gh release create.
---

# Release Notes

## 1. Collect commits

```bash
LAST_TAG=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)
git log "$LAST_TAG"..HEAD --oneline
git log "$LAST_TAG"..HEAD --format='%H%n%B%n---'   # full bodies, for BREAKING CHANGE footers
```

If there is no tag yet, use `git log --oneline` and ask the user which commit to start from.

## 2. Group

| Prefix | Section |
|--------|---------|
| `feat` | Features |
| `fix`  | Bug Fixes |
| `perf` | Performance |

Drop `chore`, `ci`, `docs`, `test`.

If any commit has a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer or a `!` after the type (e.g. `feat!:`), add a **Breaking changes** section at the very top.

## 3. Write

- Include every feat/fix/perf commit -- one line each, nothing dropped.
- Keep the whole document under 150 words. If the commit count makes that tight, shorten each line rather than omitting commits; if it is still impossible, tell the user the count and ask how to proceed.
- Write for customers: no file paths, no internal ticket IDs (e.g. `PLAT-1234`), no implementation jargon.
- House tone: plain, confident, no exclamation marks.

## 4. Post

Save the draft to `release-notes.md` and show it to the user. Post only after they approve:

```bash
gh release create <tag> --notes-file release-notes.md
```

`gh` authenticates via `gh auth login` or the `GH_TOKEN` environment variable. Never write a token into this file, a command, or the notes.
```

**What I changed and why:**

1. **The GitHub token is removed. Please revoke it now.** `ghp_7Qm2...` is a live credential, and you've pasted it into chats repeatedly. In a SKILL.md, it would end up in the repo and in every context the skill loads into. Rotate it at github.com/settings/tokens, then use `gh auth login` or set `GH_TOKEN` in your shell.

2. **I rewrote the description instead of using "Release notes helper."** The description is the only part of a skill that's always in context, and Claude uses it to decide when to activate the skill. A short label with no trigger phrase means the skill won't fire reliably when you ask for release notes. The new description starts with when to invoke and says what to do.

3. **"List every commit" vs. "under 150 words."** These rules conflict once a release has more than about 15 commits. I scoped "every commit" to feat/fix/perf, since your rule 2 already drops the rest. When the limit gets tight, the skill shortens lines instead of dropping commits, and it asks you if it still can't fit.

4. **Breaking-change detection and a confirmation step.** `--oneline` only shows subject lines, so it can't see `BREAKING CHANGE:` footers. I added a second `git log` that includes commit bodies. Publishing a release is public, so the skill shows you the draft before running `gh release create`.

Everything else is your instructions as written.
